children: Crude oil futures fell sharply to start the week after President Trump said the U.S. is "highly unlikely" to renew attacks on Iran as long as there was progress in negotiations regarding Iran's nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Both the WTI and Brent crude benchmarks plunged more than 15% last week after Democrats swept Congress, fuelling hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict in the Middle East.
Trump also is set to meet Qatar's prime minister at the White House on Monday.
However, the Iran foreign minister said talks had made no progress and Iran was waiting to see whether the U.S. administration would change its position following the elections.

"We remain skeptical that U.S.-Iran discussions will yield fruit... Still, if regional crude exports remain stout, the U.S. may have less reason to restart an active military campaign," EBW Analytics said in a note.

Flareups continue in the region, as a tanker was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile over the weekend while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.K. Maritime Trade Operations, and Iran-backed Houthi militants hit Saudi Aramco's offices in Riyadh in an attack, prompting retaliation from Saudi forces.
Meanwhile, Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes in their war, with Ukraine hitting Russian refineries and Russia repeatedly targeting energy and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine.

title: Crude oil plunges as Trump says renewed Iran attacks unlikely
